extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and SINGULAR users (researchers/programmers working on singularity theory and computational algebraic geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR computer-algebra library procedures used to classify and manipulate singularities, compute invariants, perform curve resolution/parametrization, versal deformations, and equisingularity computations. Each entry describes usage, assumptions, returned values, examples, and warnings for a specific procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: singularity
rubrics_metrics.description: singularity(t, l); t=string (name of singularity), l=list of integers/polynomials (indices/parameters of singularity). l= k [,r [,s [,a [,b [,c [,d]..]: k,r,s=int a,b,c,d=poly. The name of the dbm-databasefile is: NFlist.[dir,pag].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: get the singularity named by type t from the database. Return: Normal form and corank of the singularity named by type t and its index (indices) l. If the NFlist file is not in current directory, run MakeDBM first. Examples show calls like singularity("E[6k]",6) and singularity("T[k,r,s]", 3, 7, 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: A_L (A L)
rubrics_metrics.description: A_L(f); f poly OR A_L(s); s string (name of the singularity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: the normal form of f in Arnold’s list of singularities (in case 1); if called with a string, fetch normal form from database. A_L(f): compute via 'milnorcode' the class of f and return the normal form found in the database. Return: normal form. Example: A_L("E[13]") returns c2+a3+ab5+b8 and A_L(f) prints 'Singularity R-equivalent to : normal form : ...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalform
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: Arnold’s normal form of singularity with name s. Example: normalform("E[13]") -> c2+a3+ab5+b8.

rubrics_metrics.name: debug_log
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: print "messages" if level >= @DeBug. Useful for user-defined trace messages. Examples show init_debug and changing printlevel: debug_log(1,"no trace information printed"), debug_log(2,"nice for debugging scripts") and output formatting like 'Debug:(2): nice for debugging scripts'. See also init_debug.

rubrics_metrics.name: swap
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: b,a if a,b is the input (any type). Simple utility to swap two objects. Example: swap("variable1","variable2") -> variable2 variable1.

rubrics_metrics.name: modality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: the modality of the singularity. Example shows modality of a polynomial returning 0. Usage requires base ring and polynomial; compute returns integer modality.

rubrics_metrics.name: complexSingType
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: the type of the singularity as a string (e.g., 'D[4]'). Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: prepRealclassify
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure returns a list containing the modality of the singularity and the type of the singularity as a string. It is used in realclassify.lib to avoid classify() being called more than once. Example returns [0, 'D[4]'] for given polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: classifyCeq
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: classify simple hypersurface singularities in characteristic p > 0 with respect to contact equivalence. Return: string including the Tjurina number of f and its type in the classification of Greuel and Kroening. Example outputs indicate whether function defines a simple singularity and prints the tjurina number and type (e.g., 'E^0[6]:x^3+y^4').

rubrics_metrics.name: classifyicis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I is given by two generators. Purpose: Check whether the ideal defines a complete intersection singularity or not. Return: String type in the classification of Giusti,M or 'The given singularity is not simple'. Example: classifyicis(I) might return 'U_9:(...)'. Warnings in examples about dim(_) possibly wrong with mixed monomial ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semigroup (classifyci.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Semigroup(l); I is an ideal (Usage says Semigroup(l); I is an ideal)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: Computes the semigroup of the ideal I corresponding to each branch. Return: list of semigroup(s) corresponding to each branch. Example returns lists like [2,3] and [2,5] for branches. Note: usage/argument naming slightly inconsistent in docs—call with ideal I.

rubrics_metrics.name: BlowingUp
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering r=0,(x(1..n),a),dp; f irreducible in k[a]; I ideal of a curve (a as parameter). Compute: blowing-up of the curve at point 0. Return: list C of charts; each chart C[i] is a list (size 5 or 6) containing: chart index, minimal polynomial for new parameter, ideal H in k[a], map theta from new curve to old, ideal J = theta(I), and list of exceptional divisors. Example shows returned structure and entries. Use when resolving curve singularities via charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: CurveRes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: basering r=0,(x(1..n)) and V(I) is a curve with a singular point 0. Compute: resolution of the curve V(I). Return: a ring R = basering + k[a] containing a list Resolve: a list of charts Resolve[i] with entries: Resolve[i][1] ideal J of new curve, Resolve[i][2] ideal representing the map theta, Resolve[i][3] irreducible poly giving minimal polynomial for new parameter (deg gives number of branches in Resolve[i]), Resolve[i][4] sequence of multiplicities (sum over branches), Resolve[i][5] a list of integers, Resolve[i][6] HN matrix, and Resolve[i][7] (only for plane curves) development of exceptional divisors. Examples show detailed outputs and warnings about mixed ordering. Use setring s after call to access Resolve list.

rubrics_metrics.name: CurveParam
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I is an ideal of a curve C with a singular point 0. Compute: parametrization for algebraic branches of the curve C. Return: list L where L[1] is a ring rt=0,(t,a),ds; ring R contains a list Param of algebraic branches; each Param[i] is list of size 3: Param[i][1] list of polynomials, Param[i][2] irreducible minimal polynomial for parameter a, Param[i][3] integer b (upper bound for conductor of Weierstrass semigroup). Example demonstrates returned parametrizations like t3, t2, -t5 and bound 38.

rubrics_metrics.name: WSemigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: WSemigroup(X,b0); X a list of polynomials in one variable t, b0 integer (from curvepar.lib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: Weierstrass semigroup of space curve C given by parametrization X[1](t),...,X[k](t) up to bound b0. Assume: b0 is greater than conductor. Return: list M of size 5 where M[1]=list of integers (minimal generators), M[2]=integer conductor, M[3]=intvec of all semigroup elements up to some bound > conductor. Warning: works only over ring with one variable ordering ds. Example returns minimal generators and conductor.

rubrics_metrics.name: primparam
rubrics_metrics.description: primparam(x,y,c); x poly, y poly, c integer (from curvepar.lib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: x,y in k(a)[t] such that (x,y) is a primitive parametrization of a plane curve branch and ord(x)<ord(y). Return: Hamburger-Noether matrix of the curve branch given parametrically by (x,y). Example shows matrix entries; usage requires ring r=(0,a),t,ds and integer c as bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: MultiplicitySequence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is the defining ideal of a (reducible) plane curve singularity. Return: list X of charts; each chart contains the multiplicity sequence of the corresponding branch. Example returns sequences like 7,3,3,1,1,1. Use to obtain multiplicity sequences for branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacteristicExponents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is the defining ideal of a (reducible) plane curve singularity. Return: list X of charts; each chart contains the characteristic exponents of the corresponding branch. Example shows values like 7,10.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntersectionMatrix
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is the defining ideal of a (reducible) plane curve singularity. Return: intmat of the intersection multiplicities of the branches (matrix of pairwise intersections). Example prints a symmetric matrix of integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ContactMatrix
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I is the defining ideal of a (reducible) plane curve singularity. Return: integer matrix N of the contact matrix of the branches of the curve. Example returns matrix with 0 on diagonal and 1 off-diagonal for five branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: plainInvariants
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is the defining ideal of a (reducible) plane curve singularity. Return: list L of charts. For each branch j: L[j][1]=intvec (characteristic exponents), L[j][2]=intvec (generators of semigroup), L[j][3]=intvec (first components of Puiseux pairs), L[j][4]=intvec (second components of Puiseux pairs), L[j][5]=int (degree of conductor), L[j][6]=intvec (multiplicity sequence). L[last] contains intersection matrix, contact matrix, resolution graph. Example shows full output including matrices and vectors. See also other related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: versal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: miniversal deformation of Fo up to degree d (default d=100). Return: list L of 4 rings: L[1] extends basering Po with deformation parameters; L[2]=L[1]/Fo extending Qo=Po/Fo; L[3]=embedding ring of versal base space; L[4]=L[1]/Js extending L[3]/Js. In L[1] matrices stored: Js (equations of miniversal base space/obstructions), Fs (equations of versal family), Rs (lifting of syzygies Ro=syz(Fo)). If d defined, computes up to degree d. If 'any' provided and any[1] not a string, interactive version. printlevel controls verbosity (printlevel < 0 no additional output). Examples show how to access Fs, Js, Rs and sample Js/Fs outputs. Use for computing T1/T2 and equations of versal base/total space.

rubrics_metrics.name: mod_versal
rubrics_metrics.description: mod_versal(Mo,Io[,d,any]); Io=ideal, Mo=module, d=int, any=list (from deform.lib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: miniversal deformation of coker(Mo) over Qo=Po/Io. Return: list L of 4 rings similar to versal: L[1] extends basering with parameters; L[2]=L[1]/Io; L[3]=embedding ring of versal base; L[4]=L[1]/(Io+Js) ring of versal deformation of coker(Ms). In L[1] matrices: Js (obstructions), Fs (versal family of Mo), Rs (lifted syzygies). If d defined (!=0) computes up to degree d. 'any' and printlevel similar. Examples show printed informational messages (vdim Ext^2, Ext^1) and how to access Ms, Ls, Js; printlevel restored afterward. Use for versal deformations of modules/presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: lift_kbase
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: matrix A, coefficient matrix expressing N as linear combination of k-basis of M. Let k-basis have k elements and size(N)=c columns. Then A satisfies: matrix(reduce(N,std(M)),k,c) = matrix(kbase(std(M)))*A. Assume: dim(M)=0 and monomial ordering is a well-ordering or last block ordering is c or C. Example demonstrates computing module k-basis and resulting coefficient matrix A and verifies equality. Use to express vectors/polynomials in the k-basis of a zero-dimensional module.

rubrics_metrics.name: lift_rel_kb
rubrics_metrics.description: lift_rel_kb(N,M[,kbaseM,p]); N,M modules of same rank (from deform.lib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: [p a monomial] or product of all variables; N, M modules of same rank; M depends only on variables not in p and vdim(M) finite; kbaseM may be provided. Warning: assumptions not checked by procedure. Return: matrix A whose j-th column presents coefficients of N[j] in kbaseM, i.e., kbaseM*A = reduce(N,std(M)). Example shows usage with modules and provided kbaseM and verifies result. Use to lift relations to a chosen k-basis under given assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: tau_es
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f is reduced bivariate polynomial, basering has exactly two variables, is local and not a qring. Return: int, the codimension of the mu-const stratum in the semi-universal deformation base (tau_es). printlevel >=1 displays additional info. When called with additional parameter, computation of Milnor number is avoided (no check for NND). Example: tau_es((x4-y4)^2-x10) -> 42. See related procedures esIdeal, esStratum, invariants, tjurina.

rubrics_metrics.name: esIdeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: f reduced bivariate polynomial, basering has precisely two variables, is local and not qring, and characteristic of ground field does not divide mult(f). Return: if called with one parameter: list of two ideals: [1] Wahl's equisingularity ideal of f, [2] ideal of equisingularity with fixed position of the singularity. If called with more parameters: returns list of three ideals adding (3) ideal of all g such that deformation f+e*g (e^2=0) is isomorphic to an equisingular deformation with trivial equimultiple sections. Note: if conditions not satisfied returns list(0,0). Examples show calls, checks for Newton degeneracy and computing std(K[1]) and vdim(std(K[1])) and that it should equal tau_es(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: esStratum
rubrics_metrics.description: esStratum(F[,m,L]); F poly, m int, L list (from equising.lib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: F defines a deformation of a reduced bivariate polynomial f and characteristic of basering does not divide mult(f). If nv variables, first nv-2 are deformation parameters. If basering is qring, ideal(basering) must depend only on deformation parameters. L supposed to be output of hnexpansion with given ordering. If m given, compute ES over A/maxideal(m). Compute: equations for stratum of equisingular deformations with fixed (trivial) section. Return: either a list [ [ideal_ES, ideal_triv], error_flag ] or a ring extension with ES ideal and polynomial p and error flag. l format described: l[1][1]=ideal deﬁning ES stratum; l[1][2]=ideal defining part where equimultiple sections trivial; l[2]=1 if error occurred else 0. Procedure uses execute and printlevel>=2 displays additional info (HN expansion, blowup steps, elimination). Examples show outputs and usage with qring and removal of superfluous equations. Use to compute ES-stratum ideals or ring extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: isEquising
rubrics_metrics.description: isEquising(F[,m,L]); F poly, m int, L list (from equising.lib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: F defines a deformation of a reduced bivariate polynomial f and characteristic of basering does not divide mult(f). First nv-2 variables are deformation parameters. If basering is qring, ideal(basering) must only depend on deformation parameters. Compute: tests if the given family is equisingular along trivial section. Return: int 1 if equisingular, 0 otherwise. L supposed to be output of hnexpansion. If m given family considered over A/maxideal(m). Uses execute; printlevel>=2 displays additional info. Examples show isEquising returning 0 or 1 depending on input and working over Q[a,b]/<a,b>^2 if m=2.

rubrics_metrics.name: controlMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: controlMatrix (expects L = output of multsequence(hnexpansion(f))) (from equising.lib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: L is output of multsequence(hnexpansion(f)). Return: list M of 4 intmat's: M[1] contains multiplicities at respective infinitely near points p[i,j] (stored with a convention for multiple branches passing through same point), M[2] contains number of branches meeting at p[i,j], and further matrices (M[3], M[4]) not fully shown in this chunk. Use for bookkeeping multiplicities and branch counts during HN expansion/blowup algorithm. See related equisingularity procedures.
